home.title: Welcome to Ahmed GameLink
home.subtitle: Diagnose Roblox connection problems and get clear, lawful solutions — with no idle data usage and no background services.
home.start_tooltip: Runs a full sequential check: internet, DNS, TCP 443, then HTTPS to Roblox servers — at most 10 s per step and 45 s total. You can cancel at any time during the check.
home.note: The app uses zero data while idle and opens no connection unless you ask for one.
home.disclaimer: Note: this tool is lawful and safe and does not claim to bypass every kind of blocking — it only shows diagnostics and available solutions.

conn.status.done: Check finished in {seconds} s. Report below:
conn.status.cancelled: Check cancelled. You can press Retry at any time.
conn.btn.cancel_tip: Stop the check immediately and close every open connection.
conn.btn.retry_tip: Run a brand-new full check from the start.
conn.btn.export_tip: Save the report to a JSON file for sharing. All IP addresses in it are masked — safe to share.
conn.report.empty: No check has run yet. Press Start Diagnostics on the Home page.
conn.report.solutions_title: Suggested solutions (realistic — no promises of automatic bypass):
conn.data_usage: Data used by this check: sent {sent} / received {received} — by this app itself only; it does not include Roblox or any other app's traffic.
report.diag.no_internet: Result: there is no internet connection at all. The check stopped here because the remaining tests would be pointless. The problem is in your network or your provider — not Roblox.
report.diag.dns_down: Result: no DNS server responds (neither the system server nor the public ones). Your machine is on the network but name resolution is broken, so almost no site will open.
report.diag.dns_system_broken: Result: the DNS server your system uses (usually from the router) does not respond, while public servers (e.g. 8.8.8.8) work. Your machine cannot resolve site names unless you change the DNS settings.
report.diag.roblox_tcp_blocked: Result: the internet works, DNS works and returns Roblox's server address — but the direct connection to Roblox's own servers (TCP 443) is blocked or silent. In plain terms: your network/provider specifically prevents reaching Roblox. This is a common situation with some providers in Egypt.
report.diag.roblox_https_blocked: Result: the connection reaches Roblox up to the HTTPS stage but requests get cut or refused. This usually points to content/name-level filtering (SNI) or interference from security software on your machine.
report.diag.roblox_partial: Result: some Roblox services work and some are blocked. Try opening the site directly to see what actually works.
report.diag.roblox_service_issue: Result: everything works on your side, but Roblox's own servers respond with an error (HTTP 5xx). The problem is on their side, not yours — wait a bit and retry.
report.diag.all_good: Result: all checks passed — no visible blocking of Roblox from your network. If the game still does not work, the issue is most likely the client itself or your account state.
report.diag.cancelled: The check was cancelled before completion. The result is not final.
report.solution.check_cable: Check your network cable or Wi-Fi, and try reconnecting to the network.
report.solution.restart_router: Restart the router (unplug it for 30 seconds) — it fixes DNS and connectivity issues often.
report.solution.contact_isp: Contact your provider and ask whether there is an outage or temporary blocking in your area.
report.solution.change_dns: Change your device's DNS to a public resolver such as 8.8.8.8 (Google) or 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare). With working DNS the internet may return to normal — but Roblox will still not open if it is blocked at connection level.
report.solution.vpn_or_different_network: Connection-level blocking is not solved by changing DNS. Realistic options: a lawful VPN (requires a subscription and background running), or trying another network (e.g. mobile data) to confirm the diagnosis. The app does not break blocking automatically.
report.solution.try_roproxy: Try a free mirror such as roproxy.com (it fetches on your behalf from Roblox servers). It may work for limited features and does not guarantee the full game works.
report.solution.check_firewall: Check Windows Firewall or antivirus software on your machine — it may block game programs. (The app will not modify system settings itself.)
report.solution.wait_retry: Wait a bit then press Retry — the issue may be temporary on the servers' or the network's side.
report.note.honest: Honesty note: this is a diagnosis only. The app does not claim the ability to bypass every kind of blocking, and any solution above has its own requirements and possible extra data cost that you accept before using it.
netdiag.explain: Per-target round-trip-time (RTT) and packet-loss measurements — 3 ping attempts per target, sequential, at most ~40 seconds total. These measure path speed only; they are NOT a Roblox reachability test (that is the Connection Test).
netdiag.start_tip: Measures RTT and packet loss for your system's DNS server, public DNS resolvers and the main Roblox host — 3 attempts per target. You can cancel during the run.
data.explain: These numbers are the actual bytes produced by this app during checks only (requests + responses, including all TLS overhead) — measured at the socket level. They never include Roblox or any other app's traffic, and no Npcap/WinDivert or admin rights are used.
data.last_caption: Last check (smart or detailed) — reset at the start of every check:
data.session_caption: Session total (since the app was opened):
data.refresh_tip: Re-read the actual counter and show the latest numbers. (Manual refresh only — no automatic updates, to save CPU.)
data.reset_tip: Zero the session counter. Does not touch any other file or setting.
data.reset_message: The "session total" counter will be reset to zero. Continue?
data.note: Measurement honesty: counted bytes are the payload bytes at the socket boundary (including TLS encryption). IP/TCP headers per packet (~40–60 B) are not visible to the socket API and are not counted — a documented, uniform policy across all checks.
settings.language_combo_tip: Choose the interface language. The change applies immediately to every page without restarting the app.
settings.reset_tooltip: Delete the settings file and restore all defaults (including Arabic). Does not touch any other data.
settings.reset_message: All settings will be restored to defaults (the language will return to Arabic). Continue?
settings.privacy_text: This app never collects passwords, account data or IP addresses, never changes system settings without your consent, and never installs hidden certificates or network drivers.
about.title: About Ahmed GameLink
about.description: An open-source tool that helps users diagnose Roblox connectivity problems: DNS, TCP, HTTPS and latency checks, with a clear Arabic report and lawful, safe solutions matched to the diagnosis.
about.license_text: MIT — the project source is open and may be modified and redistributed under the license terms.
about.disclaimer_text: This tool provides no VPN service and claims no ability to bypass every kind of blocking. It shows diagnostics only and explains the requirements of any alternative connection method before use. System settings are never modified without explicit user consent.
about.privacy_text: No passwords or account data are logged. Any IP address appearing in diagnostic reports is masked before display or export. Settings are stored locally in the user's profile folder only.
